outcome: premalignant and malignant lesions of the uterine cervix
differentiation between squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma
cohort: Cervical samples were collected from a total of 200 females presenting to the Institute of Post Graduate Medical Education and Research (IPGME&R), Kolkata, for evaluation of cervical lesions.
finding: Liquid-based Cytology (LBC) demonstrated a 75% concordance rate with histopathological diagnosis for cervical lesions, and both p40 and p63 immunomarkers showed a statistically significant difference in mean percent positivity between non-neoplastic and precursor/neoplastic lesions, proving useful in differentiating squamous cell carcinoma from adenocarcinoma of the cervix.
cross-section timing: October 2020 to March 2022 (one year and six months)
